The '''2003 World Championship''' was the 8th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] at Dragon*Con in Atlanta, Georgia, over the convention's Labor Day weekend (29 August – 1 September 2003).<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref><ref name="dcon">[https://fancons.com/events/info/5400/dragon-con-2003 Dragon*Con 2003], FanCons.com (convention dates 29 August – 1 September 2003)</ref><ref name="pc-0905">[http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm SWCCGPC.com] (news of 5 September 2003: World Championship results, top 8 with deck pairs, Dragon*Con, Atlanta). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20031008101333/http://www.swccgpc.com/interior.htm Internet Archive]</ref> [[Jonny Chu]] defeated [[Greg Shaw]] in the final; the Players Committee's results give his decks as "Combat / Senate".<ref name="awards" /><ref name="pc-0905" /><ref name="tfn-2003" /> A third-place match was played, in which [[Clint Hays]] took 3rd over [[Bastian Winkelhaus]]; a forum poster recalls 2003 as the only year this was done.<ref name="pc-0905" /><ref name="f75427-1301004">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1301004#p1301004 Post by allstarz97], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (3 June 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html#p1301004 Internet Archive]</ref> The field size has not been found.

The constructed pool was printed Decipher cards through [[Theed Palace]] plus the original [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|Players Committee Virtual Sets]] then legal. The wiki files it under [[Premiere - Original VS5]], from the newest virtual cards in the published lists; a numbered cutoff for the event has not been confirmed.

== Results ==

Final places 1–8 and each player's deck pair, as announced by the Players Committee in its news of 5 September 2003 and repeated by TheForce.Net on 7 September.<ref name="pc-0905" /><ref name="tfn-2003">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/SWCCG_World_Championship_Results_announced_61552.asp SW:CCG World Championship Results announced], TheForce.Net (7 September 2003): final results 1st–8th with decks</ref> Two 2020 forum posts give the same top 8.<ref name="f75427-1300380">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300380#p1300380 Post by allstarz97], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html#p1300380 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="f75427-1300387">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300387#p1300387 Post by Yoshi], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html#p1300387 Internet Archive]</ref> The Dark and Light columns link the published wiki decklists; Chu's are his Day 2 lists, not the Combat / Senate pair he won with.

=== Top 8 bracket ===

The quarterfinal and semifinal pairings and game results have not been found. The 3rd/4th place match (Hays def. Winkelhaus) is the only placement game recorded besides the final.<ref name="pc-0905" /><ref name="f75427-1301004" />
